clue.text: Perhaps wife's earnings docked by fellow director's principal deputy

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a wife's pay may be a household's second income
a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the principal, or leading, letter of the word director's

explanation.surface: A director's chief deputy finds a spouse's pay cut by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' trims the last E from SECOND INCOME, leaving SECONDINCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is the officer who stands in for the leader, a deputy.

clue.text: Equipment in lab coat, value uncertain

indicators.note: letters whose order is uncertain may be arranged in any way

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure what a laboratory coat is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' rearranges COAT and VALUE into the answer. 'Equipment in lab' looks like part of the picture of a lab coat, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoclave is a pressurised steam vessel used in laboratories to sterilise apparatus.

clue.text: Source of oil to provide power in my area

indicators.note: power is set inside the exclamation

parts.note: 'my!' and 'cor!' are both exclamations of surprise
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A request for energy in one's own district comes from an oil producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside COR, giving COPR, then A follows. COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, which is pressed to yield coconut oil.

clue.text: Out to provoke more fondness?

definitions.meaning: a playful nod to the saying that absence makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder', so being away is what provokes more fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is not present, away from where they would be expected.

clue.text: Following the right path to have been accepted as student?

definitions.meaning: keeping to the correct route, as a ship or project might

definitions.text: to have been accepted as student?
definitions.meaning: a student admitted to a programme of study is on a course

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a student enrolled on a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan proceeding as intended is on track, keeping to its planned route.

clue.text: One struggling poet turns and runs

indicators.note: the poet's name turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot was a poet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A poet keeps spinning round and running about, struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' signals reversal of the poet's surname; 'runs' looks like part of the surface verb but gives the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiler is a person who labours hard, one who struggles at their work.

clue.text: Highly desirable books man secures with mould on the front

indicators.note: the mould is placed before the rest of the answer

parts.note: must is mould or mustiness

indicators.note: the man holds the books inside himself

parts.note: he is a man
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible, a set of books

explanation.surface: A collector thinks old books with a bloom of mould on the cover are greatly prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' signals a container; 'on the front' fixes the mould at the start. AV for books is the Authorized Version of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-have is something considered essential to own, highly desirable.

clue.text: A Republican, noticed without case, sent back with the rest

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is sent back, read in reverse
the outer letters, its case, are stripped from the word

parts.note: noticed means detected

explanation.surface: A Republican spotted without his briefcase was sent home along with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without case' strips the outer Ds from DETECTED, leaving ETECTE; A + R + ETECTE is then 'sent back' to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the other things', used to mean all the rest.

clue.text: Complaint I agree officer must accept

indicators.note: the officer takes in the agreement, holding it inside

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
amen is said to express assent

explanation.surface: A soldier grumbles that the officer has to take his agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must accept' signals the officer abbreviation taking the word of assent inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is an expression of grief or regret, a complaint in the sense of a mournful cry.

clue.text: Ominous sign once seen with regret to be actualised

parts.note: comets were once regarded as omens of disaster
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A dark portent appears, accompanied by remorse, and it is made real.
explanation.definitionFit: To come true is to happen in reality, as a hope or prophecy might, so to be actualised.

clue.text: Football fan, maybe, dropping one drink for another

indicators.note: the fan lets one drink fall away from the front

parts.note: a football fan is an example of a supporter
a sup is a mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A football fan swaps one drink for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' signals the removal. The definition 'another' means another drink, following on from 'one drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, so it is another drink beside the sup taken away.

clue.text: Be likely to possess ultimate in flair and fashion

indicators.note: the verb holds the letter within itself

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be likely to do it

indicators.note: the ultimate, or final, letter of flair

explanation.surface: Something is probably going to have the last word in style and fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to possess' puts R, the last letter of 'flair', inside TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a prevailing style or fashion of the moment.

clue.text: Being rather stupid is more than one should have to bear

definitions.meaning: somewhat dim-witted, slow on the uptake

definitions.text: is more than one should have to bear
definitions.meaning: describes something unreasonable or excessive, beyond what is fair

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British colloquialisms: 'thick' means stupid, and 'a bit thick' also means unreasonable or too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for dim, so mildly thick means rather dim-witted.

clue.text: Appreciate class course at Oxford passed very quickly

parts.note: a set is a class or group, especially of pupils
Greats is the Oxford University course in classics
tore by means rushed past

explanation.surface: Someone values a class on an Oxford course that flew past.
explanation.walkthrough: GREATS is the informal name for the classics degree at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is to value it highly, to appreciate it.

clue.text: Fact: one with six legs is upright on four

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a fact
an ant is an insect, which has six legs

explanation.surface: It is a fact that an insect stands upright on all fours.
explanation.walkthrough: Statant is a heraldic term for an animal shown standing with all four feet on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a beast described as statant stands erect with all its feet on the ground.

clue.text: Shave one's skin

parts.note: to shave is to cut
one is I, and the 's is read as S

explanation.surface: Shaving one's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical name for the skin, especially its true layer, the dermis.

clue.text: Consent to struggle, its outcome preordained?

indicators.note: letters that struggle are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a fight whose result was fixed in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to struggle' rearranges CONSENT and TO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest with a certain result is a walkover, called no contest because it is no real competition.

clue.text: Russian front I served on

indicators.note: the letter is placed on, in front of, the next piece

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A soldier recalls serving on the Russian front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served on' puts I before VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a common Russian first name, used as a byword for a Russian.

clue.text: Take all someone's cash, working alone in card manoeuvre

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the card move

parts.note: to cut is to divide a pack of cards

indicators.note: letters set working are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A card sharp operating alone fleeces a mark with a sleight of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of 'alone', and 'in' places the result inside the card manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean someone out is to take all their money, as in gambling.

clue.text: Aggressive move: army commanders hurled orders at the front

indicators.note: the letters at the front of each of these words

explanation.surface: In an aggressive move, army commanders barked out orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a showy, aggressive masculinity.

clue.text: Sweetener in a box, mild

parts.note: to spar is to box
tame means mild, gentle

explanation.surface: An artificial sweetener comes in a mild-looking box.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial low-calorie sweetener.

clue.text: Block is dull to look at

parts.note: dead means dull, lifeless
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: A wooden block is uninteresting to the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A deadeye is a round wooden block with holes, used in a ship's rigging to tighten shrouds.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, a deadeye is a pierced wooden block used to tension rigging.

clue.text: Parish priest's stipend pronounced criminal

indicators.note: the word for the stipend is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: a stipend is an income
bent is slang for crooked, criminal

explanation.surface: A vicar's pay is declared to be crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' means only the sound of INCOME is used, spelt INCUM. BENT is British slang for corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the holder of a church benefice, such as a rector or vicar of a parish.

clue.text: Devastate a fort, wounding a number inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An army ruins a fortress, injuring its garrison within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' looks like part of the battle, but it means a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea for Two is a popular song, and a number is a song or musical piece.

clue.text: Clamour to make 16 perhaps sound a laugh

indicators.note: the first word is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: to make tea, which 16 is an example of, is to brew
ha ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: Making a pot of tea seems to be followed by a noisy guffaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 16-down is TEA FOR TWO, which offers tea; making tea is to brew, heard as BROU.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or uproar, a clamour.

clue.text: Suppressing quote "Kinky sex is thrilling"

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold down the other word inside them
kinky means twisted, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Someone quotes the line that kinky sex is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' twists the three letters of 'sex' to EXS, and 'Suppressing' holds the quote inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that excites someone stirs them up, so it is thrilling them.

clue.text: The old guard become vital

parts.note: to turn is to become, as in turn sour
key means vital, crucial

explanation.surface: The old guard become indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old guard' looks like a group of veterans, but it means an old-fashioned word for a jailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnkey is an archaic word for a jailer, a prison guard who holds the keys.

clue.text: Workers stick up for the royal family

parts.note: TU is the trade union, a body of workers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Workers make a stand for the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROD to DOR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal dynasty of England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Wind temperature over port, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: port is an example of wine

explanation.surface: A gusty wind sweeps over a warm harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to wind or twist something round, as a vine does.

clue.text: Works hard to release head in waterproofs

indicators.note: the first letter is let go from the word

parts.note: toils means works hard

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to free their head from wet-weather gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release head' drops the T from TOILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils is short for oilskins, waterproof garments made of oiled cloth.
